llm_generation.text:
The solution has the right basic idea—Dora must travel around the gray square either clockwise or counterclockwise—but it incorrectly treats every choice as having probability \(1/4\).

At the starting interior intersection \(A\), she has 4 possible directions, but after moving to a side intersection, she has only 3 possible directions available. Thus each valid four-step circuit has probability

\[
\frac14\left(\frac13\right)^3=\frac{1}{108}.
\]

There are two such circuits, clockwise and counterclockwise, so the desired probability is

\[
2\cdot \frac{1}{108}=\boxed{\frac{1}{54}}.
\]

Also, the statement that these are the only four-step paths returning to the start should be justified in the solution.
